explanation: The implementation uses WP_HTML_Tag_Processor (the low-level lexical scanner) rather than WP_HTML_Processor, because the HTML Processor explicitly does not support any elements inside a TABLE — it aborts early when encountering them. The approach: (1) use next_tag('TABLE') to find the first table opener, then (2) scan all subsequent tokens with next_token(), which visits text nodes (#text) and tag openers/closers alike. A state machine tracks three variables — whether we're in a cell ($in_cell), the accumulating cell text ($current_cell), and the current row array ($current_row). Tag tokens for TR, TD, TH, and TABLE drive state transitions: a <tr> saves any open cell/row and starts a new row; <td>/<th> implicitly closes the previous cell (if any) and opens a new one; </td>/</th> explicitly closes the cell; </tr> closes the cell and saves the row; </table> flushes everything and breaks the loop. Text tokens are appended to $current_cell while $in_cell is true, with get_modifiable_text() providing the already-decoded text (character references resolved). TBODY/THEAD/TFOOT tags are encountered in the token stream when present but require no state-machine action. The API methods used are: WP_HTML_Tag_Processor constructor, next_tag(), next_token(), get_token_type(), get_tag(), is_tag_closer(), and get_modifiable_text().
